situations.situation: executing a plan or a stated goal (building a slice)

quotes.chongdae:run: Never do the subagent's work yourself and never edit its answer: the record says the session relayed it, and a relay that edits is a lie.
quotes.hacheong:hire: A session dispatching its own subagent instead (a `native:` provider) runs the same argv with `--prompt-only`, gives the printed prompt to a fresh subagent, and writes its JSON answer verbatim to the response path.

findings.why: Both tell the session how to relay a `native:` provider dispatch: run the argv with --prompt-only, give the prompt to a fresh subagent, and write its JSON answer verbatim without doing or editing the work. Following either one gives the same result.

class_quote.quote: Never do a member's work yourself and never edit its answer.

quotes.chongdae:run: Commit a task's work with the subject `run-<id>/<task> (session): <what>`
quotes.hacheong:build: Do not commit, branch, or touch the run's record (`.chongdae/`), the plan, or anything under the user's home directory.

findings.why: The build worker is told never to commit, while the run skill tells the agent to commit a task's work. The two instructions go to different actors at different times: the hired worker leaves its work uncommitted in the tree, and the session commits it afterwards, before close.

class_quote.quote: commit the *work* (code, tests, documents) as usual, before `close`.

quotes.file:AGENTS.md:
Use that skill when hiring members; maintaining the plugin does not
itself call a member.
quotes.chongdae:run: In a session run the lock says who does a task: `add <id> --check …` goes to the lock's `implementer` (a fresh process builds it from the brief and checks)

findings.why: In this repository, AGENTS.md says maintaining hacheong does not itself call a member. A chongdae run that executes a maintenance plan here sends every checked task to the lock's implementer, which is a hired hacheong member. The session can take the work itself only with a recorded reason. Whether maintenance slices here should be hired or self-performed is a person's call.

proposed.accept: AGENTS.md only says maintenance is not inherently a hiring act; within a chongdae run the lock decides who builds, and a self-performed task needs the person's word via --role session --why

situations.situation: reviewing or disputing a change before merge

quotes.plugin:chongdae: the run is the agent's container, so Edit/Write are refused until one starts
quotes.dwitbuk:review: A review run by hand is a record like a run: commit `reviews/<id>.json`.

findings.why: The chongdae mode makes a run the only container for writes and refuses them when no run is in progress. A review run by hand before a merge, which is the case where dwitbuk is not chongdae's reviewer, still writes reviews/<id>.json and tells the agent to commit it outside any run. A commit is hard to undo, and neither text says whether this record is exempt from the run requirement or needs a run of its own.

proposed.accept: A hand review's reviews/<id>.json is written by the dwitbuk engine, not through Edit/Write; a person decides whether committing it outside a chongdae run is allowed or whether a session run must be started first

quotes.dwitbuk:eyes: Read the contract sections against the diff (Read the touched files and the tests under target when the diff is not enough).
quotes.hacheong:quibble: You dispute the contract before anyone builds on it.

findings.why: Both are fresh-process disputers that read the contract sections and the checks and report quoted findings against them. A person disputing a change before a merge could reach for either one.

class_quote.quote: You are the verifier of one slice, before its gate. The checks passed; that is a premise, not a verdict.

situations.situation: testing or trying a built slice

quotes.plugin:chongdae: the run is the agent's container, so Edit/Write are refused until one starts
quotes.hacheong:nitpick: `tests` lists every file you wrote or changed.

findings.why: The nitpick worker has to write test files. The chongdae mode refuses Edit/Write when no run is in progress, and a worker started by a role gets the modes too.

class_quote.quote: Silent in a worker session (AGENT_WORKER=1): the run is the hiring session's.

quotes.hacheong:nitpick: You write the tests that will decide a contract, before anyone builds it, and you write them to make the builder fail.
quotes.hacheong:newbie: For a program you try to use it the way its README says, in a scratch directory, and you write down what happened.

findings.why: Both workers claim to test or check a slice. One writes the contract's tests and the other tries the program, so for a built slice the two could be hired for the same job.
findings.class-refused: sequenced claimed; its sentence is not in hacheong:hire's text

quotes.file:AGENTS.md: `python3 -m unittest test_native_prompt.py test_hostcall_env.py test_record_paths.py test_red_gate.py` from this directory ([Self-check](README.md#self-check)); neither makes model calls.
quotes.hacheong:hire: Use when a plan or the lock names a hacheong role (build, quibble, nitpick, newbie) as a task's provider, or when the person asks who can build, dispute, test or try a slice.

findings.why: In this source repository there are two ways to test a change. AGENTS.md says to run the self-checks, which make no model calls. The hire skill says to hire the nitpick or newbie member.

class_quote.quote:
Use that skill when hiring members; maintaining the plugin does not
itself call a member.

quotes.plugin:jokbo: jokbo: at session start, a map of what this project holds (documents, and a line from each product that declares one) and how to ask; at the first look at a file, a line per fact that bears on it; when another hand changes the project between this session's calls, a line saying what.
quotes.hacheong:newbie: You do not open anything that person would not see (source files, tests, records) — if you learn how it works from the inside, you are no longer the person this role exists for.

findings.why: The newbie only works if it knows nothing about the project's internals. jokbo's mode says nothing about staying quiet in worker sessions, so it would hand the newbie a map of the project and facts about files.

quotes.plugin:chongdae: the run is the agent's container, so Edit/Write are refused until one starts

findings.why: After a slice, mangsang:operate has the agent write a proposals.json file into the project and record relations. chongdae refuses Edit/Write when no run is in progress, so writing the proposals file assumes a run is open. If the slice's run has already closed, the write is refused.

class_quote.quote: the run is the agent's container, so Edit/Write are refused until one starts

situations.situation: asking what happened or what is open

quotes.dwitbuk:review: Use when the session-start line says objections are undisposed, when the person asks what happened or what is open, before a merge, or on a project whose lock has no `reviewer` role (there, run the review by hand).
quotes.jokbo:read: what happened in that run / today
quotes.chongdae:run: To know what happened in a run — before a retrospective, or to pick up where a run stopped — `show` (`--run ID`, `--since REV` for a line per run, `--path FILE` for the tasks that touched a file), not the record's JSON.

findings.why: All three say they answer 'what happened': dwitbuk gives review findings and open objections, jokbo gives document sentences and commits, and chongdae gives the run record through `show`. Each gives a different answer, and no text says which comes first or which one yields.

quotes.dwitbuk:review: A review run by hand is a record like a run: commit `reviews/<id>.json`.
quotes.chongdae:run: Writes to the project need a run in progress (the PreToolUse hook refuses them otherwise).

findings.why: To answer 'what is open' on a project with no reviewer role, dwitbuk runs a review by hand, writes dispositions and commits `reviews/<id>.json`. chongdae says writes to the project need a run in progress. Asking what is open does not start a run, so dwitbuk's record write and commit happen outside any run.

proposed.accept: dwitbuk's review record is written by its own engine, not by the agent's Edit/Write, and is committed alone as a record commit. Committing it outside a run needs the person's word.

situations.situation: asking about past decisions or what stands on a file before changing it

quotes.jokbo:read: **Everything that stands on a file**: `file PATH` — the sections that speak of it with how current each is, who last changed it, and what each declared `file` read says.
quotes.mangsang:operate: Before editing a registered file: `lookup <path>` prints the confirmed relations standing on it — grouped by concept with its meaning, each with its quote, its confirmer and whether it is fresh now — and marks which ones the edit would make stale; read it instead of opening the record's JSON.

findings.why: Both claim to answer 'what stands on this file before I change it'. mangsang's plugin manifest declares its `file` read as `mangsang.py lookup {path}`, so jokbo's `file PATH` already includes mangsang's lookup output as one of the declared reads, along with document sections and the file's last author. Running both prints the mangsang relations twice.

class_quote.quote: **Everything that stands on a file**: `file PATH` — the sections that speak of it with how current each is, who last changed it, and what each declared `file` read says.

situations.situation: setting up a project's tooling for the first time

quotes.plugin:chongdae: the run is the agent's container, so Edit/Write are refused until one starts
quotes.hunsu:compose: an edit to `hunsu.json` (`engines`, `resolutions`, `local-hooks-ok` for a hook the whole team runs)

findings.why: When a project is set up for the first time, compose writes hunsu.json and hunsu.local.json. chongdae refuses Edit/Write until a run exists, so compose's edits fail if no run has been started.

class_quote.quote: the run is the agent's container, so Edit/Write are refused until one starts

quotes.plugin:chongdae: the run is the agent's container, so Edit/Write are refused until one starts

findings.why: When a project first adopts mangsang, operate writes files such as people.json and proposals.json. chongdae refuses Edit/Write until a run is started.

class_quote.quote: the run is the agent's container, so Edit/Write are refused until one starts

quotes.hunsu:compose: Calls to skills outside the lock are refused by hunsu's own PreToolUse hook.
quotes.mangsang:operate: when a project first adopts mangsang

findings.why: During first-time setup, operate expects to be callable when the project adopts mangsang. compose's hook refuses any skill that is not in the lock, so operate is refused until mangsang has been added to the manifest and the lock is rebuilt.

class_quote.quote: If the user wants such a skill, that is a manifest change: `hunsu add`, then lock again.

situations.situation: agent environment differs from or is missing the lock

quotes.hunsu:compose: Write what they chose and run step 1 again.
quotes.plugin:chongdae: the run is the agent's container, so Edit/Write are refused until one starts

findings.why: To re-lock a drifted environment, compose has the agent write the user's choices into hunsu.json or hunsu.local.json (and edit `engines`, `resolutions` or `local-hooks-ok`). chongdae refuses Edit/Write when no run is in progress, so compose's write step fails unless a chongdae run has already started.

class_quote.quote: the run is the agent's container, so Edit/Write are refused until one starts
